title: POC Sizing & Hosting Playbook — Northshore Utilities
summary: Initial POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and timeline for a customer-facing inference feature. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, security controls (VPC, KMS, SOC2), cost-band estimates, and a phased pilot plan with a 6-8 week guarded timeline.
topics: Success criteria: latency, accuracy, cost per request, uptime
Workload sizing: peak RPS, average tokens per request, KV cache hit rate assumptions
Benchmarks: throughput targets, p95/p99 latency goals, sample datasets and scripts
Deployment modes: Hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem
Security & compliance: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
Timeline and next steps: benchmark sprint, pilot kickoff, pricing and contract

[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, this is Diego from our solutions engineering team.
[00:14] Priya (CTO): thanks, maya. quick intro — Northshore is building a conversational assistant for our outage reporting and customer billing flow. main concerns are latency during peak and keeping customer data inside our env.
[00:28] Diego (SE): great, so we'll run through sizing, the benchmark plan, and then talk hosting options and security.
[00:41] Elliot (Platform): i'm mostly curious about cost and autoscale behavior; we have spikes up to 120 RPS for small bursts and a steady 10 RPS baseline.
[00:55] Maya: perfect, we'll capture that. can you confirm average tokens per request?
[01:03] Owen (Data Scientist): typical user message ~60 tokens, we then generate a 120 token response on average. but for diagnostics it can be up to 400.
[01:18] Fatima (Security): two quick must-haves: data never leaves our VPC for PII, and we require KMS integration plus audit logs for every inference call.
[01:30] Diego: noted. Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and HSM/KMS integrations; Dedicated can also be put in a VPC peering arrangement with dedicated pools. our hosted offering encrypts at rest and in transit but we understand that's a blocker for some regulated data.
[01:55] Speaker 1: (background) uh-huh
[02:05] Maya: let's zoom into success criteria. what does success look like for you at the end of the pilot?
[02:11] Priya: three things: 1) p95 latency under 300ms for typical flows, 2) accuracy of intent classification within 4% of our baseline, and 3) predictable cost — i.e., no surprise spikes.
[02:27] Diego: ok p95 300ms is reasonable as a pilot target — is p50 or p99 also useful?
[02:34] Elliot: p99 under 800ms would be nice, we can tolerate occasional long tails.
[02:40] Owen: and for accuracy we'll run our 10k prompt eval set.
[02:48] Maya: good. we'll propose a benchmark run that measures tokens/sec at different concurrency, p95/p99 latencies, and a downstream accuracy run using your eval set.
[03:00] Priya: timeline question: how long to get meaningful results?
[03:05] Diego: typical benchmark sprint is 2 weeks for initial performance runs, then a week to tune batching/quantization and another 1–2 weeks for a canary rollout. so 6–8 weeks end-to-end for pilot.
[03:23] Fatima: does that differ between hosted and private?
[03:27] Diego: yes. hosted is fastest — we can run hosted benchmarks in a few days using our curated models. Dedicated requires provisioning GPU pools and can take 1–2 weeks to provision reserved capacity. Private on-prem adds network and KMS integration time — 2–4 additional weeks depending on procurement.
[03:48] Elliot: what about cost delta? do you have ballpark numbers per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated?
[03:55] Maya: roughs: hosted higher per-token but no infra commit; Dedicated lowers unit cost by 30–50% depending on committed utilization; Private has similar unit costs to Dedicated but includes infra+support fees. we'll share a modeled cost spreadsheet.
[04:12] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[04:20] Diego: sizing note — with 120 RPS spikes and 180 tokens per total per transaction, at steady 10 RPS you need capacity for baseline plus headroom. for Dedicated we'd recommend starting with a 2-card pool (A100 class) with autoscale policies, or for lower cost 4x8-bit quantized V100-like instances if the model supports it.
[04:44] Owen: we plan to use an LLM similar to the open Llama-v3 family — quantization is on the table. how does Redwood handle kv cache and re-use across requests?
[04:55] Diego: we have prefix caching and KV cache strategies; for chat sessions we can reuse cached K V to reduce token compute. small transcripts: cache hit assumptions of 20–40% can cut token cost meaningfully.
[05:12] Priya: for PII are we ok with token logging? we only want anonymized logs or no customer text logged.
[05:20] Maya: we can disable transcript retention on the hosted side for the pilot, or route logs to your syslog when on private. Dedicated also supports customer-controlled retention.
[05:34] Fatima: SOC2 report and ISO attestation — can you provide evidence?
[05:40] Maya: yes, we will share SOC 2 Type II and our compliance pack. for Private deployments you get additional auditability and you can bring your own KMS/HSM.
[05:53] Diego: technical deep dive — sample benchmark plan: 1) synthetic throughput runs across 1, 5, 25, 100 concurrency; 2) real workload replay using Northshore traces; 3) accuracy eval with 10k set; 4) failure injection to validate fallback to a smaller model.
[06:18] Elliot: fallback is important — we don't want total outages during traffic bursts. what's the fallback latency?
[06:24] Diego: a smaller model fallback hits lower throughput but can be much cheaper; typical fallback model p95 may be ~2x latency of primary but keeps the app responsive.
[06:34] Priya: can you route by policy, e.g. critical flows go to Dedicated while low-risk flows hit Hosted?
[06:41] Maya: yes that's supported. Smart routing can send by route/model/customer tier. you can pin critical routes to Dedicated or Private and let less sensitive routes use hosted to save cost.
[06:56] Owen: about telemetry — we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency. is that in the console?
[07:02] Diego: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-model & per-route dashboards, traces and error analysis. some labels are auto-tagged but you can add route metadata for billing.
[07:14] Speaker 3: (brief)
[07:20] Priya: a question on SLAs — what's guaranteed for Dedicated?
[07:24] Maya: Dedicated comes with an SLA on availability and latency targets in the contract; hosted has best-effort guarantees but service credits are possible at enterprise tiers. Private has contractual SLAs too but depends on your infra.
[07:38] Fatima: we will need RBAC and SSO/SAML for the Console.
[07:42] Diego: supported — role-based controls, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and audit logs for all management operations.
[07:51] Elliot: can we run a smoke benchmark on hosted to sanity-check our expected latencies before committing infra?
[07:58] Maya: absolutely. we can run a 48-hour hosted benchmark using a sandbox model and your sample traces. after that, you can decide whether to move to Dedicated or Private.
[08:08] Priya: ok, important to quantify cost per 1k requests as well.
[08:13] Maya: yes we'll include cost per 1k requests and cost per 1M tokens in the spreadsheet.
[08:20] Owen: about model versions — can we pin to a specific model version and roll forward?
[08:25] Diego: yes — model versioning and canary rollouts are supported. you can roll out by % and auto-fallback if output drifts or latency increases.
[08:39] Priya: data residency — our customers are mostly in the EU, but we have US operations. can you guarantee region routing?
[08:47] Maya: hosted supports region selection for data residency; Dedicated and Private can be deployed in region-specific infra to meet residency requirements.
[08:56] Fatima: procurement question: what's typical lead time for Dedicated procurement?
[09:01] Maya: depends on contract and MSA negotiation, typically 3–6 weeks for paperwork plus provisioning time. Private often takes longer because we coordinate with your infra team.
[09:14] Elliot: do you have benchmark scripts we can run ourselves? we prefer to run at least one baseline internally.
[09:20] Diego: yes we will share the benchmark harness (k6 + custom token driver) and a reproducible dataset. we also share a calibration guide for sequence lengths, batch sizes, and kv cache warm-up.
[09:36] Owen: for tuning, what batch sizes do you recommend?
[09:40] Diego: depends on latency SLO. for sub-300ms p95 on moderate sequence lengths, small batch sizes (1–8) plus continuous batching works well. for throughput optimization you push to 16–64 but latency rises.
[09:56] Priya: can you write down the pilot success metrics so procurement can review?
[10:00] Maya: yes, we'll submit a one-pager.
[10:06] Speaker 4: (typing)
[10:12] Diego: quick note on cost modelling — we factor in cache hit rate, average token length, and committed utilization. a 30% cache hit can reduce token compute cost by roughly the same fraction depending on your request shape.
[10:27] Priya: sample acceptance criteria please — will you include roll-forward stop gates?
[10:31] Maya: we'll propose: gate 1 after benchmark (meets latency & accuracy targets); gate 2 after 2-week canary (observed error rates <1% and no P0s); go/no-go for full rollout based on cost model and SLOs.
[10:46] Fatima: on the security playbook — will the SOC2 package include network diagrams?
[10:50] Maya: yes. we provide architecture diagrams, encryption details (TLS, KMS), and our incident response summary. Private gets deeper logs.
[11:00] Elliot: competitor question — how do you compare to Anthropic/others for dedicated workloads?
[11:06] Diego: many providers offer managed models; Redwood differentiates by runtime optimizations for high throughput, smart routing, and tooling to measure unit economics — plus the Dedicated/Private parity so the same runtime works across modes.
[11:25] Priya: Ok. let's talk concrete next steps.
[11:30] Maya: propose we do: 1) share benchmark harness and cost model by EOD Tue, 2) run a 48-hour hosted smoke test with Northshore traces (you supply sanitized trace) — target next week, 3) plan Dedicated sizing if hosted looks promising.
[11:50] Owen: we can sanitize traces and share by Friday.
[11:54] Fatima: i'll review the SOC2 artifacts once you send.
[11:59] Diego: action items we'll note — and schedule a kickoff call for the benchmark sprint.
[12:08] Priya: sounds good. any other questions?
[12:12] Speaker 5: (brief)
[12:20] Maya: quick clarifying note — for the hosted smoke we'll disable transcript retention and enable anonymized logging as you requested.
[12:30] Priya: thank you.
[12:34] Maya: we'll follow up with an email summarizing scope, owners, and timelines. thanks all.
